Rashi on Kiddushin 36a:10:1.hebrew: תפילין גופייהו מהכא גמירי - כלומר, ההיא ג"ש דבין עיניכם מיבעי ליה למגמר מקום תפילין מהכא, דלא תימא בין עיניכם ממש, דהיינו על פדחתו; אלא יליף מבין עיניכם דקרחה, דבמקום שער — דבלאו מקום שער לא משכחת קרחה — והיינו למעלה מפדחתו:
Rashi on Kiddushin 36a:10:1.english: Phylacteries themselves are derived from here - That is to say, that gezeirah shavah of "between your eyes" is needed by him to derive the placement of phylacteries from here, so that you should not say [it means] literally "between your eyes," which is on his forehead; rather, he derives [it] from "between your eyes" [stated regarding] baldness, which is in a place of hair — for without a place of hair you do not find baldness — and that is above his forehead.

Rashi on Kiddushin 36a:11:1.hebrew: ובין לאביי ובין לרבא - דנפקא להו פטורא דנשים מקרא אחרינא — ״בנים אתם״, מאי דרשי ביה:
Rashi on Kiddushin 36a:11:1.english: And according to both Abaye and Rava - Since they derive the exemption of women from another verse — [as for] “You are sons,” what do they derive from it?

Rashi on Kiddushin 36a:13:1.hebrew: וכ"ת סכלי הוא דמקרו בני - כשאין בהם אלא שטות הוא דמיקרו בנים, אבל כשהם רשעים, דלית בהו הימנותא, לא מקרו בנים:
Rashi on Kiddushin 36a:13:1.english: And if you would say: It is [only when they are] foolish that they are called sons - It is [only] when there is nothing in them but foolishness that they are called sons, but when they are wicked, in that they have no faithfulness, they are not called sons.

Rashi on Kiddushin 36a:14:1.hebrew: וכ"ת סכלי הוא דמקרו בני - כשאין בהם אלא שטות הוא דמיקרו בנים, אבל כשהם רשעים, דלית בהו הימנותא — לא מקרו בנים:
Rashi on Kiddushin 36a:14:1.english: And if you would say: It is [when they are] foolish that they are called sons - It is [only] when there is nothing in them but foolishness that they are called sons, but when they are wicked, such that there is no faithfulness in them, they are not called sons.

Rashi on Kiddushin 36a:14:2.hebrew: משחיתים - דהיינו עבודה זרה, כדכתיב (דברים ד׳:ט״ז) פן תשחיתון ועשיתם פסל וגו':
Rashi on Kiddushin 36a:14:2.english: Who deal corruptly - That is idol worship, as it is written: “Lest you deal corruptly and make a carved image…” (Deuteronomy 4:16).

Rashi on Kiddushin 36a:14:3.english: They are not called proper sons - Ever again.

Rashi on Kiddushin 36a:14:4.hebrew: ת"ש - דהדרי מקרו בני אל חי ע"י תשובה:
Rashi on Kiddushin 36a:14:4.english: Come and hear - For they return to being called “sons of the living God” through repentance.

Rashi on Kiddushin 36a:15:1.hebrew: הסמיכות כו' - אינה סומכת, ואינה מניפה, ואינה מגשת מנחה — ואפילו היא כהנת אין העבודה כשרה בה להגיש מנחה בקרן מערבית דרומית כמשפטה, דתנינן לה בפ"ב דסוטה (דף יד:) — ואינה קומצת ומקטרת, ואינה מולקת עוף, ואינה מקבלת דם, ואינה מזה דם חטאת העוף. חוץ מסוטה ונזירה, שהם מניפות מנחתן בעצמן — בין כהנות בין ישראליות — שמנחתן טעונה תנופה בבעלים; ובגמ' יליף לה:
Rashi on Kiddushin 36a:15:1.english: The placing of hands, etc. - [A woman] does not place [her] hands [on the head of an offering], and does not wave [offerings], and does not bring near a meal-offering — and even if she is a priestess, the [sacrificial] service is not valid through her to bring near a meal-offering to the southwestern corner [of the altar] according to its law, as we learned in chapter 2 of Sotah (14b) — and she does not remove a handful, nor burn [it on the altar], and she does not pinch [the neck of] a bird-offering, and she does not collect blood, and she does not sprinkle the blood of a bird sin-offering. Except for a sota and a nazirite woman, who wave their meal-offering themselves — whether priestesses or Israelite women — for their meal-offering requires waving by the owners; and in the Gemara, it derives this.

Rashi on Kiddushin 36a:16:1.hebrew: אל בני ישראל - דויקרא, וכתיב בההוא עניינא: ״וסמך ידו״:
Rashi on Kiddushin 36a:16:1.english: To the sons of Israel - [In the book] of Leviticus; and it is written in that [same] passage: “And he shall place his hand.”

Rashi on Kiddushin 36a:16:2.hebrew: אל בני ישראל - דויקרא, וכתיב בההוא עניינא: "וסמך ידו":
Rashi on Kiddushin 36a:16:2.english: To the sons of Israel - [In the book] of Leviticus, and it is written in that passage: “And he shall place his hand.”

Rashi on Kiddushin 36a:17:1.hebrew: דבר אל בני ישראל והניף - בצו את אהרן: "המקריב את זבח שלמיו", וכתיב בההוא עניינא "והניף":
Rashi on Kiddushin 36a:17:1.english: “Speak to the sons of Israel…and he shall wave” - In [Parashat] Tzav et Aharon: “He who offers the sacrifice of his peace offerings” [Leviticus 7:29], and it is written in that context: “and he shall wave” [v. 30].

Rashi on Kiddushin 36a:18:1.english: Bring it near - From this verse we derive [the requirement of] bringing near in chapter 2 of Sotah (ibid.).

Rashi on Kiddushin 36a:1:1.hebrew: אחת היא - משמעות שתיהן — בין ביד, בין בכלי:
Rashi on Kiddushin 36a:1:1.english: Are one - The meaning of both of them [is the same] — whether [done] by hand or with an implement.

Rashi on Kiddushin 36a:21:1.english: Pinching is juxtaposed to burning - And behold, we excluded women from: “And the sons of Aaron shall burn it.”

Rashi on Kiddushin 36a:2:1.hebrew: מבני אהרן - דכתיב (ויקרא כ״א:ה׳) ״לא יקרחו קרחה בראשם״, גבי ״אמור אל הכהנים״:
Rashi on Kiddushin 36a:2:1.english: From the sons of Aaron - For it is written: “They shall not make baldness upon their head” (Leviticus 21:5), in [the passage of] “Speak to the priests” [the sons of Aaron].

Rashi on Kiddushin 36a:3:1.english: That when the verse writes - [Namely,] “The sons of Aaron.”

Rashi on Kiddushin 36a:3:2.hebrew: נשתוק קרא - מהך ג"ש גבי ישראל:
Rashi on Kiddushin 36a:3:2.english: Let the verse be silent - From this verbal analogy [gezeirah shavah] regarding Israelites.

Rashi on Kiddushin 36a:6:1.hebrew: בראשם - האמור אצל כהנים, מה ת"ל? דלפי שנאמר בישראל: ״בין עיניכם״, משמע סמוך לפדחת:
Rashi on Kiddushin 36a:6:1.english: Upon their head - [As for that which is] stated regarding priests, why does the verse state [it]? For since it is stated regarding Israelites, “between your eyes,” [this] implies adjacent to the forehead.

Rashi on Kiddushin 36a:8:1.hebrew: ומה להלן - בישראל, על מת — דהתם כתיב ״למת״:
Rashi on Kiddushin 36a:8:1.english: And just as there - In [the case of an] Israelite, [it is] over a dead person, as there it is written: “For the dead.”

Rashi on Kiddushin 36a:8:2.hebrew: א"כ - דלהך מילתא לחודה אתא:
Rashi on Kiddushin 36a:8:2.english: If so - That it came for this matter alone.

Rashi on Kiddushin 36a:8:3.hebrew: נכתוב - בתרוייהו קרח. מאי קרחה? הוה ליה כג"ש יתירה, למידרש נמי הא:
Rashi on Kiddushin 36a:8:3.english: Let [Scripture] write - In both of them, “bald” [keraḥ]. What [is the significance of] “baldness” [korḥa]? It is like a superfluous verbal analogy, to also derive this [teaching as well].

Tosafot on Kiddushin 36a:10:1.hebrew: תפילין גופייהו מהכא גמרינן להו - וא"ת: ומה בכך? מ"מ נילף קרחה מתפילין, דאין ג"ש למחצה, ונימא: מה תפילין נשים פטורות, ה"נ גבי קרחה? וי"ל: דשמא לא נגמרה ג"ש אלא לאשמועינן מקום הנחת תפילין. וקשה להר"ם: אמאי אין מניחין תפילין בכל הראש, כי היכי דקאמר קרחה בכל הראש? ושמא להכי מהני האי "בין עיניכם", דהוה מצי למכתב "בראשיכם". ואע"ג דגבי קרחה כתיב "בין עיניכם", ואפ"ה קרחה בכל הראש — וי"ל: דליגמר ג"ש נכתב:
Tosafot on Kiddushin 36a:10:1.english: "Phylacteries themselves are derived from here" - And if you say: And what of it? Nevertheless, let us derive baldness from phylacteries, for a gezeirah shavah is not applied partially; and let us say: Just as women are exempt from phylacteries, so too regarding baldness [they should be exempt]? And one can say: Perhaps the gezeirah shavah was established only to teach us the place of donning phylacteries. And it is difficult to the Ram: Why do we not don phylacteries on any part of the head, just as [the Gemara] says that baldness [applies] to the entire head? And perhaps this is what "between your eyes" accomplishes, for it could have written "on your heads." And even though regarding baldness it is written "between your eyes," and even so baldness [applies] to the entire head — one can say: it was written [there] in order to derive the gezeirah shavah.

Tosafot on Kiddushin 36a:15:1.hebrew: הסמיכות והתנופות וההגשות - נראה דמהגשות ואילך מיירי בכהנים, ואתו קראי בגמ' למעוטי כהנות; אבל סמיכות ותנופות איירי בישראל:
Tosafot on Kiddushin 36a:15:1.english: The placing of hands, and the waving, and the bringing near - It appears that from bringing near onward, [the Mishnah] is dealing with priests, and the verses in the Gemara come to exclude female priests; but the placing of hands and waving deal with Israelites.

Tosafot on Kiddushin 36a:15:2.hebrew: הקבלות והזאות - והולכה וזריקה לא קתני, דהולכה בכלל קבלה — שהרי מן "והקריבו הכהן" נפקא כמו קבלה — וזריקה בכלל הזאה. וא"ת: אמאי איצטריך קרא בגמרא למעוטי נשים? תיפוק ליה דכולהו מ"ע שהזמן גרמא הוו, שהרי אינן נוהגות אלא ביום, כדכתיב (ויקרא ז׳:ל״ח): "ביום צותו להקריב קרבניהם"! וי"ל: דמ"מ איצטריך קרא למעוטינהו ולמיפסל קרבן בנשים, דאי לאו קרא לא הוה ידעינן שהעבודה פסולה בהן; להכי איצטריך קרא למעוטי, למימר דמחללי עבודה ועבודתן פסולה. מיהו מסמיכה קשה: אמאי איצטריך קרא למעטינהו, דהא עבודה לא אתחלל בהכי? כלומר, בלא סמיכה נמי אין הקרבן פסול בכך, ואם נעשה סמיכה בנשים לא מיפסל קרבן בכך. וי"ל: דמ"מ איצטריך קרא למעוטי, דסד"א משום דכתיב "וסמך... ושחט" איתקש סמיכה לשחיטה: מה שחיטה כשרה בנשים, כדתנן בזבחים (דף לא:) ומייתי בשמעתא קמייתא דשחיטת חולין (דף ב:): "כל הפסולין ששחטו שחיטתן כשרה, שהשחיטה כשרה בזרים ובנשים וכו'" — אף סמיכה כשרה בנשים; להכי איצטריך למעוטי. ותנופה נמי איצטריך למעוטי, משום דאשכחן תנופה דכשרה בנשים, כדמפרש לקמן:
Tosafot on Kiddushin 36a:15:2.english: The collecting [of blood] and the sprinkling - And [the Mishnah] does not teach bringing [the blood] and throwing [the blood], for bringing is included in collecting [the blood] — as it is derived from "[and the priest] shall bring [the blood]" just like collecting — and throwing is included in sprinkling. And if you say: Why was a verse needed in the Gemara to exclude women? Let him derive it [from the principle] that all of these are positive, time-bound commandments, as they apply only by day, as it is written (Leviticus 7:38): "On the day that He commanded... to sacrifice their offerings"! And one can say: Nevertheless, a verse was needed to exclude them and to invalidate an offering [performed] by women, for were it not for the verse, we would not have known that the service is invalidated through them; therefore, a verse was needed to exclude [them], to say that they profane the service and their service is invalid. However, regarding the laying on of hands (semikhah), it is difficult: Why was a verse needed to exclude them, seeing that the service is not profaned by this? That is to say: even without semikhah, the offering is not invalidated thereby, and if semikhah were performed by women, the offering would not be invalidated thereby! And one can say: Nevertheless, a verse was needed to exclude [them], for you might have thought: Since it is written, "And he shall lay his hand... and slaughter," semikhah is juxtaposed with slaughter; just as slaughter is valid when performed by women — as we learned in a mishna in Zevachim (31b) and it is cited in the first sugya of [tractate] Shechitat Chullin (Chullin 2b): "All disqualified people who slaughtered, their slaughter is valid, for slaughter is valid by non-priests and by women, etc." — so too semikhah would be valid by women; therefore, it was necessary to exclude [them]. And waving also needed [a verse] to exclude [them], because we find waving that is valid for women, as [the Mishnah] explains below.

Tosafot on Kiddushin 36a:4:1.hebrew: אי לאו ג"ש ה"א הפסיק הענין - וא"ת: היכי תיסק אדעתין למימר הכי? הא מפקינן לעיל (קידושין דף לה:) מפאת שאינה בבל תשחית, ולא אמר דקרחה, שכתוב בפרשה ראשונה קודם בל תשחית, הפסיק הענין לפאת זקן, וכ"ש דקאי אקרחה, שהיא ראשונה בפרשה, קרובה יותר לבני אהרן דכתיב בפרשה! ועוד קשה: דת"ק דמתניתין היכי פליג אקרחה, דקאמר במתני' "חוץ מבל תקיף ובל תשחית", ולא קאמר "ובל יקרחו"? והא אפילו מפאת אמר לעיל דקאי אבני אהרן, כ"ש דקאי אקרחה דקרובה לבני אהרן! וי"ל: דסד"א דגבי קרחה, דאע"ג שהיא קרובה לבני אהרן, הפסיק הענין משום דכתיב (דברים י״ד:ב׳) "כי עם קדוש אתה", דמרבה נשים, ואפילו בישראל; ומפרש בגמרא דלא הפסיק הענין:
Tosafot on Kiddushin 36a:4:1.english: Were it not for the verbal analogy, I would say that the matter was interrupted - And if you will say: How could it enter our minds to say this? For did we not derive above (Kiddushin 35b) from "the corner of" [pe'at] that [a woman] is not [included] in "do not destroy" [the corners of the beard], and [the Gemara] did not say that [the prohibition against] baldness, which is written in the passage first, before "do not destroy," interrupted the matter for the corner of the beard; and all the more so that [the exclusion of "the sons of Aaron"] applies to baldness, which is first in the passage, closer to "the sons of Aaron" written in the passage! And furthermore, it is difficult: How does the First Tanna of our Mishnah disagree regarding baldness, as he says in the Mishnah: "Except for [the prohibitions of] do not round [the corners of the head] and do not destroy [the corners of the beard]," and does not say "and they shall not make baldness"? For even regarding "the corner of" [the beard], [the Gemara] said above that [the exclusion of "the sons of Aaron"] applies to it; all the more so that it applies to baldness, which is closer to "the sons of Aaron"! And one can say: It would enter our minds to say that regarding baldness, even though it is closer to "the sons of Aaron," the matter was interrupted, because it is written (Deuteronomy 14:2): "For you are a holy people," which includes women, even among Israelites; and the Gemara explains that [due to the verbal analogy] the matter was not interrupted.

Tosafot on Kiddushin 36a:8:1.hebrew: אם כן ליכתוב קרא קרח - פי': וליתן את האמור של זה בזה הוה מפקי במה מצינו. ואי משום דריבה בהו מצות יתירות — אין לנו לחלק מצוה אחת שאנו מוציאין בכהנים ובישראל בהדיא; דודאי גוף המצוה לא היינו לומדים, אבל פירוש המצוה גמרי שפיר מהדדי:
Tosafot on Kiddushin 36a:8:1.english: If so, let the verse write "bald" [keraḥ] - Explanation: And [as for] applying that which is stated in this [passage] to that [passage], we would have derived [it] through a mah matzinu. And if [one were to argue that an analogy cannot be made] because [Scripture] multiplied additional mitzvot for [priests] — we do not differentiate a single mitzvah that we find explicitly both regarding priests and regarding Israelites; for certainly we would not have derived the substance of the mitzvah [from one to the other], but the definition of the mitzvah we derive well from each other.
